title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines Redwood Inference’s standard processes and manager responsibilities for hiring, onboarding, performance reviews, and continuous feedback. It consolidates our approved templates, scorecards, and timelines so hiring managers and people-ops partners can run predictable, equitable, and high-quality people processes.

Scope
-----
Applies to all full-time and long-term contract hires, hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and people leaders in engineering, product, and go-to-market functions. Does not replace role-specific interview rubrics maintained by each department; instead it provides the canonical end-to-end process and manager responsibilities.

Key principles
--------------
- Candidate experience: transparent timelines, timely communication, and clear expectations.
- Hiring for outcomes: focus on competencies and measurable signals (scorecards).
- Inclusive and equitable process: diverse panels, standardized questions, and unbiased feedback collection.
- Fast and deliberate: aim for high quality while minimizing time-to-offer. Standard target: 28 days from opening to offer for most IC roles.

1) Hiring process (manager checklist)
----------------------------------
1. Partner with people-ops to finalize role brief and compensation band. (Owner: hiring manager)
2. Draft role rubric (top 3 success metrics) and preferred/required skills. Share rubric with panel.
3. Create job posting and sourcing plan. Confirm diversity sourcing channels.
4. Kick off interview panel and schedule training on inclusive interviewing (if needed).
5. Triage candidates weekly with recruiter; update scorecard for every interviewed candidate.
6. After onsite/loop, convene debrief within 48 hours, collect numeric scores and written notes.
7. Calibrate with hiring committee (if role > L4 or manager-level) and get approval to extend offer.
8. Work with people-ops on offer letter, relocation (if applicable), and background checks.
9. Communicate outcome to candidates within the agreed SLAs: rejection within 3 business days; offer acceptance window standard 7 calendar days.

Interview stages and recommended timing
--------------------------------------
- Phone screen (30 min) — recruiter or hiring manager — confirm fit, salary expectation, right-to-work, and role basics.
- Technical/skills screen (45–60 min) — pair-programming or take-home assessment depending on role.
- Onsite/loop (3–5 interviews, total 3–4 hours) — competency-based interviews across these areas: 1) Technical depth, 2) System design or product sense, 3) Execution and ownership, 4) Collaboration & culture add.

Interview panel composition guidance
----------------------------------
- At least one peer-level interviewer and one cross-functional interviewer.
- Include a representative from diversity hiring pool where possible.
- For senior hires, include a manager or director-level interviewer.
- Avoid conflicts of interest (e.g., direct reports of the hiring manager).

Scorecard (required for every interview)
--------------------------------------
Use the standardized numeric scorecard (1–5) plus written evidence. Each candidate’s final recommendation must include: average numeric score, top strengths, top concerns, and hiring manager recommendation (hire/no-hire/strong-hire).

Example scorecard table (copy into ATS or meeting notes):
| Competency | Weight | Score (1–5) | Evidence (short) |
| Technical depth | 30% | 4 | Implemented async task queue; described tradeoffs |
| System design | 25% | 3 | Good high-level design; lacked latency considerations |
| Execution & ownership | 25% | 5 | Owned infra migration project; shipped end-to-end |
| Collaboration & culture | 20% | 4 | Clear cross-team communication examples |
Final recommendation: Strong hire — average 4.0

Offer & negotiation
-------------------
- People-ops owns the offer letter generation and compensation approval. Hiring manager to provide business justification for exceptions.
- Standard sign-off: hiring manager -> people-ops -> finance (for incremental headcount or band exceptions) -> legal (if necessary).
- Target response times: 24 hours internal approval on standard offers; 48 hours if non-standard compensation or relocation is involved.

2) Candidate rejection and debrief process
-----------------------------------------
- Rejections should be empathetic and specific where possible (e.g., “We were looking for deeper experience in X”).
- Provide constructive feedback only when the candidate requests it and when interviewers can provide concrete examples. People-ops coordinates feedback delivery.

3) Employee onboarding (first 90 days)
-------------------------------------
Onboarding owner model
- People-ops: new hire paperwork, benefits, payroll setup, access provisioning coordination.
- Hiring manager: role onboarding, 30/60/90 plan, check-ins, team introductions.
- IT/Infra: hardware provisioning and VPN/VPC access.

Pre-boarding (before day 1)
- Send welcome email with first-day logistics, org chart, and 30/60/90 expectations.
- Order hardware and confirm delivery date.
- Create base Slack, email, and internal accounts; request access to required repos and tools.

Day 1–7 (orientation + role ramp)
- Day 1: orientation overview (People-ops) — benefits, payroll, handbook review, security training.
- Manager: 1:1 to review role goals, immediate priorities, and team norms.
- Deliver hardware, grant access, and schedule key introductions (product manager, tech lead, buddy).

Week 2–4
- Complete role-specific training modules and product orientation.
- Assign first project: scoped to deliverable within 30 days (small but meaningful).
- Weekly 1:1 with manager.

30/60/90 plan template (manager fills with candidate-specific goals)
- 30 days: learning goals, documentation to review, first minor deliverable.
- 60 days: contribute to feature or process, pair with 1–2 team members.
- 90 days: full ownership of a project area, peer feedback cycle.

Buddy program
- Assign a buddy for the first 90 days. Buddy responsibilities: cultural orientation, quick answers to logistics, and at least two check-ins per week for the first month.

Access and security checklist (to be completed by IT + manager)
- Laptop provisioned: YES/NO
- MFA enrolled: YES/NO
- VPN and internal network access: YES/NO
- Repos and dashboards access: list repos
- KMS/HSM access (if needed): request submitted

4) Performance and feedback cycle (annual + ongoing)
----------------------------------------------------
Annual cycle (timeline)
- Goal setting window: Q4 planning for next year (company goals + team goals).
- Mid-year check-in: end of Q2 (formal written update).
- End-of-year review: performance rating, calibration, and compensation recommendations (Q4).

Continuous feedback
- Encourage monthly 1:1s and quarterly upward feedback. Use our Slack feedback channel and 360 templates for cross-functional input.
- Managers should document coaching conversations and expected outcomes in the performance system.

Performance ratings and calibration
- Ratings scale: 1 (below expectations), 2 (meets some expectations), 3 (meets expectations), 4 (exceeds expectations), 5 (exceptional).
- Calibration panels run by people-ops ensure consistency across teams. Calibration includes data: objective achievements, manager write-ups, peer feedback, and impact examples.

Improvement plans and exits
- For sustained underperformance, managers should: 1) document concerns and set measurable improvement goals, 2) partner with people-ops for a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) if issues are not resolved in informal coaching windows (typically 30–60 days), 3) escalate to HR/People-ops for next steps.

5) Manager responsibilities (detailed)
-----------------------------------
Hiring
- Own role rubric, interviewing panel, and final hiring recommendation.
- Ensure interviewers are trained, available, and provide timely feedback.

Onboarding
- Prepare 30/60/90 plan before day 1.
- Prioritize early wins and assign an appropriate first project.

Performance
- Hold regular 1:1s and document feedback.
- Run calibration-ready reviews and provide concrete examples to support ratings.

Coaching & career development
- Maintain a development plan for each direct report and document promotion-readiness signals.
- Conduct promotion calibration annually or when manager recommends promotion; use people-ops promotion rubric.

Offboarding
- Complete checklist with IT and people-ops: revoke access, conduct exit interview, and capture knowledge transfer.

6) Templates and artifacts (copyable)
------------------------------------
- Candidate scorecard (trustworthy numeric + narrative): use interview-scorecard template in our ATS.
- Hiring brief: role summary, business impact, top 3 success metrics, compensation band.
- Offer justification memo (for non-standard comp).
- 30/60/90 plan template (Google Doc).
- Feedback templates: mid-year summary, promotion memo, and PIP template.

7) Equity, diversity & inclusion checkpoints
-------------------------------------------
- Diverse slate policy: at least one candidate from an underrepresented group in final 3 for technical roles.
- Panel diversity: when feasible, include at least one interviewer from a different background or function.
- Interview question fairness: all candidates asked core competency questions; avoid questions that probe protected characteristics.

8) Metrics & SLAs (people-ops dashboard)
----------------------------------------
- Time-to-offer (median): target 28 days.
- Offer acceptance rate: target > 70% for IC roles.
- New hire 90-day retention: target > 95%.
- Onboarding completion (first 14 days): target 100% for required trainings.
- Performance calibration completion: 100% before compensation cycle closes.

9) FAQ and common scenarios
---------------------------
Q: What if a hiring manager needs to extend an expedited offer?
A: Contact people-ops; we can prioritize approvals and arrange a shorter acceptance window. Document reason for expedite in the hiring brief.

Q: How do we handle counter-offers?
A: Document market data and consult people-ops. We evaluate counter-offers case-by-case based on role criticality and internal parity.
